data.title: Meta's Non-Voting Stock Insulates Zuckerberg's Voting Rights — Market Talk
data.description: Meta's decision to create a new class of non-voting stock is likely a gambit to protect CEO Mark Zuckerberg's voting rights ahead of California's proposed one-time billionaire tax, Oppenheimer analysts write in a note. Assuming Zuckerberg is on the hook to raise $15 billion to pay the tax, and Meta needs to raise another $150 billion over time to fund its AI infrastructure, his voting stake could dilute from 60.6% to 56.3%, they say. The dilution would be much less if Meta does not issue additional equity, suggesting to the analysts that equity issuances are on the horizon. "While still greater than 50%, creating non-voting stock creates a buffer if the company had to rely on a greater mix of equity vs. debt," they write. (elias.schisgall@wsj.com)

data.title: Nasdaq ticks up as tech stocks steady; SpaceX worries hit telecoms
data.description:
Key points:
  • Indexes: Dow down 0.95%, S&P down 0.11%, Nasdaq up 0.32%
  • SLB gains after Q3 profit beat
  • Telecoms down, while tower operators rise on report of SpaceX wireless carrier talks
  • S&P 500 energy sector climbs to record high, tracking jump in oil prices

By Tharuniyaa Lakshmi and Ragini Mathur

The tech-heavy Nasdaq edged higher on Friday, helped by signs of stabilization in some tech stocks, while telecom shares tumbled on concerns that SpaceX's entry in the sector could heighten competition and threaten their market share.

For the week, the benchmark S&P 500 and the Nasdaq were on track for losses, while the blue-chip Dow remained slightly higher, supported by gains in defensive stocks.

The Philadelphia Semiconductor index rose 1.4%, as some chip-related stocks gained on Friday. Nvidia was up 0.3%, while Micron Technology and Intel gained 2.5% and 3.8%, respectively.

AI-related shares swung sharply this month, first coming under pressure over CoreWeave's debt burden and the cost of financing AI investment.

On Thursday, the Nasdaq fell again, logging the biggest single-day drop in four months. The slide accelerated following Meta's nearly 8% decline after the company reported its first cash outflow in more than a decade amid concerns over its AI-related expenditures.

CoreWeave shares were down 2.3% on Friday.

"Investors are still trying to wrap their heads around the sheer size of this AI spend. The sheer size of these notional dollars is staggering, but we aren't at the point of the cycle yet that we've seen this return," said James O'Day, head of equities at Citizens Bank.

"The market's probably healthier than it feels."

The S&P 500 communication services index was down 0.6%, as AT&T , Verizon and T-Mobile fell between 1.3% and 5.6% after a report said SpaceX was in talks with cellular infrastructure companies about launching a nationwide wireless carrier program. SpaceX shares gained 2.2%.

US cell tower operators gained from this news, with Crown Castle up 11.11% and American Tower up 4.8%.

Market focus remains on the earnings season, with major companies such as Microsoft , Alphabet and Amazon reporting next week.

At 12:02 p.m. ET, the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 502.87 points, or 0.95%, to 52,365.11, the S&P 500 CBOE:SPX lost 8.60 points, or 0.11%, to 7,654.90, and the Nasdaq Composite gained 80.59 points, or 0.32%, to 26,091.45.

Eight of 11 sectors on the S&P 500 declined, while the energy index rose to a record high, tracking gains in oil prices, and the information technology sector rose 0.9%.

Brent crude held near a more-than-five-month high amid Middle East supply concerns, adding to inflation worries ahead of the Federal Reserve's policy meeting next week.

Markets expect the Fed to keep interest rates unchanged at its meeting next week, according to the CME's FedWatch Tool.

Data from the University of Michigan showed US consumer sentiment edged down near a record low in October, as rising prices because of the Middle East conflict soured households' views of the economy.

S&P 500's third-quarter profit growth is now forecast at 32.3%, up from 30.7% previously, according to LSEG data.

Among major movers, Comfort Systems was the biggest loser on the benchmark index, with a 7.5% fall, despite its third-quarter revenue and profit beating estimates.

Bloom Energy dropped 11.4% even after the energy firm raised its fiscal 2026 forecast.

SLB rose 7% after the oilfield services provider beat Wall Street estimates for third-quarter profit.

Declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 1.85-to-1 ratio on the NYSE and by a 1.54-to-1 ratio on the Nasdaq.

The S&P 500 posted 17 new 52-week highs and 6 new lows, while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 54 new highs and 276 new lows.

data.title: SBI Reassures Customers On Funds As Data Exposure Comes Under Scrutiny
data.description:
The lender has contacted customers whose information appeared in exposed records and commissioned a cybersecurity investigation to establish the extent of the breach

State Bank of India (SBI) has begun direct communication with customers whose information surfaced in a recent cyber incident, seeking to limit the risk of subsequent fraud and reassure depositors about the security of their funds.

The public sector lender said on October 23 that it had contacted affected customers through email and WhatsApp. The communication follows the identification of customer information in records reportedly discovered on the dark web. “ We reiterate that your account balances and funds are safe with us,” SBI said in its statement.

The bank also urged customers to exercise caution while using digital banking services, particularly against unsolicited communications that seek confidential credentials. “Customers are advised to follow safe digital banking practices, never share their OTP, PIN or password with anyone, and remain vigilant against suspicious calls, messages and emails,” the lender said.

Investigation To Establish Exposure

The incident has raised concerns about the potential misuse of customer information, even as SBI maintains that account balances and funds remain secure. A preliminary assessment of approximately 3.75 lakh records reportedly found on the dark web identified 3,897 customer records containing personally identifiable information. The information included details such as names, mobile numbers, dates of birth, email addresses and residential addresses, along with customer identifiers and loan-related information.

SBI has engaged an independent cybersecurity agency to examine the incident and determine the nature and extent of the exposure. The investigation will be important in establishing how the information became accessible, whether the exposed records are authentic and what additional safeguards may be necessary.

Risk Of Targeted Fraud

The exposure of personal information can create opportunities for fraudsters to impersonate financial institutions and craft communications that appear credible to customers. Such attempts may seek to obtain banking credentials or persuade recipients to disclose sensitive information.

SBI has therefore urged customers not to share one-time passwords (OTPs), personal identification numbers (PINs) or passwords, irrespective of the identity claimed by a caller or sender. The bank’s assurance on account balances addresses concerns about the immediate safety of customer funds. However, the investigation will need to establish the full implications of the reported data exposure and whether further remedial measures are required.

data.title: Isha, Akash Ambani Turn 35, Lead Reliance’s Retail And Telecom Businesses
data.description:
The twins have moved into key leadership roles at Reliance Industries, with Akash steering Jio’s telecom business and Isha leading Reliance Retail as the conglomerate enters a new phase of succession

Isha and Akash Ambani, the twins of Reliance Industries chairman Mukesh Ambani and Nita Ambani, turned 35 on Friday, October 23, marking another milestone in their growing leadership roles across the conglomerate’s telecom and retail businesses.

Born on October 23, 1991, the siblings have evolved from next-generation representatives of the Reliance group into key figures overseeing two of its largest consumer-facing businesses.

Both joined Reliance’s boards in 2014 and have since been closely involved in the group’s expansion across digital services, telecommunications and retail. They also played a role in discussions that brought global technology companies, including Meta and Google, into Jio Platforms.

Akash Ambani Leads Jio’s Telecom Push

Akash took over as chairman of Reliance Jio Infocomm in June 2022. Since its commercial launch in 2016, Jio has reshaped India’s mobile data market through affordable connectivity and has grown into one of the country’s largest telecom operators.

Akash has been involved in shaping Jio’s products and digital services since its early years. His leadership comes as the business broadens its ambitions beyond connectivity into technology and digital services.

Jio’s proposed public listing also places the business in the spotlight, with the company’s future growth and valuation likely to remain closely watched by investors.

Isha Ambani Steers Reliance Retail

Isha was elevated to lead Reliance Retail shortly after Akash’s appointment at Jio. The business spans grocery, fashion, electronics and consumer brands, giving it a broad presence across India’s retail market.

At Reliance’s 2022 annual general meeting, Isha announced the group’s entry into the fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) segment. Her responsibilities have also included branding and marketing across Jio and Reliance Retail, placing consumer engagement and brand-building at the centre of her role.

Reliance Retail’s expansion reflects the group’s wider strategy of strengthening its consumer businesses across multiple categories.

A New Generation Takes Charge

The twins’ leadership roles reflect a broader generational transition at Reliance Industries, where the next generation is taking greater responsibility for key growth businesses while Mukesh Ambani continues to guide the group.

For the advertising and marketing industry, Jio and Reliance Retail are particularly significant because of their scale, brand visibility and partnerships. Decisions on positioning, consumer engagement and business expansion across these companies can influence wider market trends.

As they enter their 35th year, Isha and Akash face the task of sustaining growth across two highly competitive sectors while helping shape the next phase of Reliance’s business strategy.

BW Businessworld wishes the twins a very happy birthday.

data.title: IndiGo Extends Saudi Flight Cancellations, Riyadh Services Suspended Till 31 October
data.description:
Flights to and from Jeddah, Dammam, and Madinah will remain cancelled until 27 October as the airline monitors the security situation

IndiGo has extended the cancellation of flights to and from four Saudi Arabian cities amid security concerns. Flights connecting India with Riyadh will remain cancelled until 31 October, while services to and from Jeddah, Dammam and Madinah will remain suspended until 27 October.

The airline announced the extensions on Friday 23 October, as it continues to assess the evolving security situation. Affected passengers are being notified through the contact details provided at the time of booking. IndiGo has advised travellers to check their flight status before heading to the airport.

Security Concerns In Saudi Arabia

The latest extension follows an attack at King Fahd International Airport in Dammam on Wednesday that killed an Indian national and injured two others. Another Indian national was injured in a separate attack at Saudi Aramco’s Shaybah oilfield on the same day.

The disruptions come amid heightened security concerns following attacks targeting Saudi Arabia’s airports, energy installations and other critical infrastructure. Airlines have been adjusting their schedules as they monitor developments and coordinate with authorities.

Other Indian carriers have also extended suspensions on Saudi routes. Air India and Air India Express have suspended flights on all routes to Saudi Arabia until 24 October, while Akasa Air has extended its suspension until 27 October.

IndiGo has asked passengers whose bookings were made through travel partners to contact those partners directly for assistance. Travellers are advised to verify their flight status and check with the airline for the latest updates before travelling.

data.title: Trump's diesel price relief efforts grow costlier as election nears
data.description:
Key points:
  • $8 billion farm aid pushes payments to a record $55.4 billion
  • Analysts see little diesel price relief before midterms
  • Russian fuel deal risks aiding Moscow with little US benefit

By Jarrett Renshaw and Leah Douglas

With the November midterm elections fast approaching, President Donald Trump is throwing an array of costly and politically fraught solutions at one stubborn problem: the price of diesel.

His administration has offered billions of dollars to farmers, relaxed rules for truckers, eased sanctions on Russian fuel and pressured European allies to release emergency stocks. Yet diesel prices rose again last week, leaving Trump spending political and financial capital without delivering the relief his party wants as voters go to the polls.

Republicans are defending narrow majorities in Congress, and high costs are a major concern for voters. Nearly 80% of Americans blame Trump for higher costs, according to an October Reuters/Ipsos poll.

US diesel prices rose nearly 10 cents a gallon in the latest week to an average of $6.28, reversing two weeks of declines and remaining near record highs, according to the Energy Information Administration.

Diesel in the last two months has become a central issue not only in the midterms but as a catalyst driving up already-elevated US inflation. The fuel is critical for farmers, construction companies, freight operators and more, and government data last week showed its rise was partly behind hefty increases in delivery costs, early-stage food production costs and even toy prices.

The political pressure is particularly acute in traditionally Republican Farm Belt states like Iowa and Kansas, where rising fuel and fertilizer costs, trade disruptions and weak farm economics have fueled discontent among some of Trump's core supporters.

Trump has promoted his diesel measures at campaign rallies across the region. He signed an executive order onstage in Nebraska allowing red-dyed diesel to be used in highway vehicles and announced $8 billion in new farm aid during a rally in Kansas on Monday.

The measures illustrate the trade-offs Trump is accepting in pursuit of near-term relief. The new aid adds fresh strain on federal spending, while the Russian fuel move risks helping Moscow finance its war in Ukraine. Pressure on European allies to release emergency stocks, backed by a threat to restrict US diesel exports, has created diplomatic friction.

“The president tends to discount long-term losses over short-term gain, and I am skeptical if there is any short gain to be had here,” said Chris Borick, a pollster and political scientist at Muhlenberg College in Pennsylvania.

The White House attributed high diesel prices to “pre-existing issues,” including years of refinery closures and damage from Russia's war in Ukraine, while defending Trump's efforts to ease costs.

“The President wants diesel prices to fall, which is why he has taken historic actions to save American farmers, truckers, and workers every hard-earned penny," White House spokeswoman Taylor Rogers said.

SKEPTICISM AND UNANSWERED QUESTIONS

One of Trump's most direct attempts to lower diesel costs has struggled to gain traction.

Trump signed an executive order this month allowing truckers to use red-dyed diesel, typically intended for off-road use such as farm equipment, for highway driving while temporarily avoiding certain federal tax reporting and record-keeping requirements.

But the IRS has not eliminated the federal diesel tax, instead temporarily waiving related reporting requirements and penalties through year-end, leaving uncertainty for truck stops and fuel sellers.

David Fialkov, top lobbyist at NATSO, a trade group representing the largest US truck stop operators, said members appreciate Trump's effort to tackle diesel costs but that the guidance remains "murky" and carries too much risk.

"I really don’t see any of these dyed diesel announcements making a meaningful dent in diesel prices," Fialkov said.

Trump is also turning to federal payments to cushion some of the constituencies feeling the pain.

Government payments to farmers were already expected to top $47 billion this year, buoyed by commodity payments and $12 billion in tariff relief distributed by the US Department of Agriculture earlier this year. The $8 billion farm relief program would push the total to a record $55.4 billion, exceeding the previous high of $45 billion in 2020, when farmers received pandemic assistance.

The payments can help farmers manage higher costs and lost sales but do not directly address the market disruptions driving up fuel and fertilizer prices. They also raise questions about taxpayer spending to compensate producers for damage that farm groups say is linked partly to the administration’s own trade and foreign policies.

“This is the second round of emergency aid this year to address losses that were largely foreseeable,” National Farmers Union President Rob Larew said. “Trade disruptions and rising fuel costs tied to conflict abroad have put family farmers in a difficult position, and one-time payments can't provide the stability they need to plan for the future.”

The aid will arrive after the November 3 election, and likely not reach farmers until the end of the year, USDA official Richard Fordyce told Reuters on Friday.

FRICTION OVER RUSSIAN FUEL

Some of Trump's efforts to increase diesel supplies carry geopolitical trade-offs.

His decision to ease sanctions on Russian diesel that were designed to restrict Moscow’s energy revenues and limit its ability to finance its war in Ukraine has drawn bipartisan criticism — and raised questions about whether the move will meaningfully lower US fuel prices.

Trump has defended the sanctions relief as necessary to draw Russian President Vladimir Putin into negotiations to end the war in Ukraine and to release American prisoner Stephen Hubbard.

As the administration's intervention efforts have failed to lower fuel costs, Trump has sought to shift blame toward Ukraine and President Volodymyr Zelenskiy rather than the Iran war ahead of the elections.

Analysts say the Iran conflict has been the much bigger driver of the diesel price spike, disrupting global oil flows and refined-fuel supplies, while Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries have helped tighten supplies but played a more limited role in the price.

“I sort of see it as a blame-shifting kind of scapegoating operation, more than a genuine attempt to moderate prices in the lead-up to the election,” said Edward Fishman, director of the Maurice R. Greenberg Center at the Council on Foreign Relations.

data.title: Cathie Wood Makes Surprise Move Across Three Popular Tech Stocks
data.description:
Cathie Wood's ARK Invest bought heavily into Meta Platforms after the stock's post-earnings selloff, while reducing exposure to Palantir and Roblox (RBLX).

ARK funds purchased 38,110 Meta shares worth about $24.7 million on Thursday, Oct. 22, after the stock plunged roughly 7% and erased its gains for the year.

At the same time, Wood sold 7,936 Palantir shares worth about $1.55 million and unloaded 33,793 Roblox shares valued at roughly $1.8 million.

The moves come as the three stocks sit in very different places.

Meta's selloff followed a quarter in which revenue jumped 26% year over year to $64.6 billion, helped by stronger advertising and engagement. But investors focused heavily on rising AI spending after the company lifted the lower end of its 2026 capital-expenditure outlook to $135 billion, leaving the range at $135 billion to $145 billion.

That spending pressure has become harder to ignore, particularly with Meta's free cash flow turning negative for the first time since 2012, according to TipRanks.

Palantir, meanwhile, remains one of the market's strongest AI winners.

Second-quarter revenue increased 93% to $1.94 billion, while U.S. commercial revenue surged 149%. The company also raised its full-year revenue outlook to roughly $8.15 billion to $8.158 billion.

But after a roughly 1,111% three-year rally, expectations are already extraordinarily high.

Roblox presents a very different setup.

The stock remains down about 58% over the past year, with investors still questioning profitability, growth and monetization. Second-quarter bookings increased just 8%, while the company guided for a 14% to 18% decline in Q3 bookings.

Investor Takeaway

I think the interesting part of ARK's move is the contrast in valuation and sentiment.

Meta was bought immediately after investors punished the stock for rising AI costs, while Palantir was trimmed after one of the strongest multiyear rallies in the market.

That does not necessarily mean Wood has turned bearish on Palantir or Roblox.

But the size difference is notable: ARK bought nearly $25 million of Meta while selling only about $3.3 million combined across the other two names.

That makes the trade look more like a meaningful buy-the-dip move in Meta than a wholesale exit elsewhere.

For investors, the key things to watch are Meta's AI spending and monetization, Palantir's ability to keep beating elevated expectations, and whether Roblox can stabilize bookings and improve monetization.

Cathie Wood appears willing to lean into Meta while much of the market is focused on the cost of its AI ambitions.

data.title: Sigma Lithium Extends 4-Year US$100 Million Senior Secured Debt to June 2027; 7,090t Produced Since Restart
data.description:
HIGHLIGHTS

  • Sigma Lithium extends the maturity of its 4-year US$100M senior secured debt with Synergy Capital by six months, from December 2026 to June 2027.
    • The interest rate on the senior secured facility remained unchanged at SOFR + 6.95% p.a., as did the covenants and events of default.
  • The extension defers Sigma Lithium's repayment by six months, enabling the Company to continue ramping up production and building operational cash flow before the new debt maturity date in June 2027.

  • Since operations restarted on October 5, 2026, the Company has produced 7,090t of lithium oxide concentrate up to October 22 , 2026.

  • Sigma Lithium maintains its target to scale its annualized production of lithium oxide concentrate to 330,000 tonnes by year-end 2027.

  • The extension follows a reduction in total debt over the past two years:

    • Repaid more than US$90M in debt since 2Q 24 through cash generation.
    • Reduced total debt by approximately 40% over the past two years, to US$125M as of October 21, 2026.

Toronto, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - October 23, 2026) - Sigma Lithium Corporation (BVMF: S2GM34), the largest industrial-mineral lithium oxide concentrate producer in the Americas¹, dedicated to supplying global battery producers with sustainable and traceable lithium materials and its subsidiary, Sigma Mineracao S.A. ("Sigma Lithium" or the "Company") have signed an agreement letter to extend the maturity ("Extension Agreement") of its US$100 million in outstanding senior secured debt with Synergy Capital ("Synergy") by six months, from December 2026 to June 2027. The interest rate on the senior secured facility remained unchanged at SOFR + 6.95% p.a.

The extension defers the Company's debt final repayment requirement in December 2026, as a result enabling Sigma Lithium to lengthen 93% of its debt profile to June 2027, enhancing its financial flexibility, supporting its execution plans.

The extension gives the Company time to ramp up production following the restart of operations:

  • The Company recommenced operations on October 5, 2026, after the Federal Superior Court granted a decision reinstating all its environmental licenses.
  • The Company produced 7,090t of lithium oxide concentrate between October 5 and October 21, 2026.

Sigma Lithium maintains its target to scale its annualized production of lithium oxide concentrate to 330,000 tonnes by year-end 2027, supported by the Company's existing industrial capacity at its Cleantech Industrial Plant and its recycling and reprocessing circuits ("Cleantech Industrial Plant").

Sigma Lithium will report 3Q 26 production, sales, realized prices, costs and cash by November 13, 2026.

The extension follows a reduction in total debt over the past two years:

  • Repaid more than US$90M in debt since 2Q 24 through cash generation.
  • Reduced total debt by approximately 40% over the past two years, to US$125M as of October 21, 2026.

The Extension Agreement maintains similar covenants and events of default as the original senior secured debt agreement dated December 2022.

Ana Cabral, Chief Executive Officer and Co-Chairperson of Sigma Lithium, stated: "We appreciate the constructive engagement and continued support of Synergy Capital extending our maturity profile ahead of schedule. The six-month extension provides additional time to continue ramping up production ahead of the new maturity date. We have produced more than 6,400 tonnes of high-grade lithium oxide concentrate in the two weeks since operations resumed as we continue to ramp up production."

Ms. Cabral added, "Over the past two years, we have repaid more than US$90 million in debt. Together with our low costs and current lithium pricing levels, we expect to regain operational cash flow momentum. Thanks to the hard work of our teams and the trust of our stakeholders, our capital structure enhances our resilience and flexibility as we work toward our 2027 targets."

SIGMA LITHIUM IS AN ECONOMIC ENGINE IN THE JEQUITINHONHA VALLEY, ONE OF BRAZIL'S MOST DISADVANTAGED REGIONS

Sigma Lithium supports 19,000 jobs and approximately 80,000 family members. The Company's economic impact can be seen in the triple-digit GDP growth of towns in the Vale do Jequitinhonha (Lithium Valley), where it operates across 12 municipalities:

  • Araçuaí's GDP per capita grew by 123% and Itinga's by 110%, during the same period.
  • Araçuaí had the highest GDP per capita in the region, surpassing even larger municipalities such as Teófilo Otoni, which has a population four times larger.
  • Economic growth is further demonstrated by the opening of 9,410 new companies between January 2023 and March 2026.
  • Details of Sigma Lithium's social programs in the Vale do Jequitinhonha, including Dona de Mim, Zero Drought, Water for All and Education that Transforms, are available at https://sigmalithiumcorp.com/social/.

SIGMA LITHIUM HAS GENERATED SHARED PROSPERITY IN THE VALE DO JEQUITINHONHA

The scale of Sigma Lithium's social initiatives reflects their impact in the Vale do Jequitinhonha. These initiatives began before the Company commenced operations.

The Company has supported voluntary programs promoting economic inclusion, access to water, food security, education, and drought resilience since before it began generating revenue:

  • Dona de Mim: More than 2,000 women have become entrepreneurs through Sigma Lithium's microcredit opportunities, supporting approximately 10,000 family members.

  • Zero Drought: A total of 1,400 rainwater collection and irrigation structures ("Barraginhas") were built to strengthen drought resilience for approximately 5,600 small-scale subsistence farmers.

    • These initiatives support approximately 22,400 rural family members.
  • Water for All: Enabled access to drinking water for 100% of Sigma Lithium's neighboring community.
  • Education that Transforms: Sigma Lithium renovated and helped build local schools, sports facilities, and a childcare center, including a state-of-the-art SESI STEM school.
    • These initiatives support educational and extracurricular programs for approximately 776 children, expanding future opportunities for them and approximately 1,500 parents.

The qualified person (QP) for the technical information contained here is Mr. Alexandre Rodrigues Cabral, P. Eng., member of the Ordre des Ingenieurs du Quebec (OIQ, membership number 105796), who is considered, by virtue of his education, experience and professional association, a Qualified Person under the terms of NI 43-101. Mr. Cabral is not considered an independent QP under NI 43-101 as he is a Sigma Lithium Director and Chair of the Company's Technical Committee. Mr. Alexandre Rodrigues Cabral has reviewed and approved the technical and scientific content of this release.

ABOUT SIGMA LITHIUM

Sigma Lithium Corporation (BVMF: S2GM34) ("Sigma Lithium" or "the Company") is the largest industrial-mineral producer of lithium oxide concentrate in the Americas¹ and is dedicated to industrializing socially and environmentally sustainable lithium materials to supply global producers of batteries for energy security. The Company runs one of the world's largest lithium production sites-the fifth largest industrial-mineral complex for lithium oxide concentrate-at its Grota do Cirilo operation in Brazil. Sigma Lithium currently has a nameplate capacity to industrialize 330,000 tonnes of lithium oxide concentrate on an annualized basis at its mine and state-of-the-art Cleantech Industrial Plant.

Sigma Lithium is at the forefront of environmental and social sustainability in the battery materials supply chain. Its Cleantech Industrial Plant combines nearly 100% water reuse, zero use of toxic chemicals, no tailings mud dams, and 100% renewable electricity. For more than three years, Sigma Lithium has recorded no lost-time accidents.

The Company plans to resume its Phase 2 expansion in 2027, which is designed to nearly double annual production capacity to 580,000 tonnes. It also plans a Phase 3 expansion to increase capacity further to 830,000 tonnes. For more information about Sigma Lithium, visit our website.website

data.title: Mark Zuckerberg Faces $11 Billion Question With Unexpected Answer
data.description:
California's proposed billionaire tax is already having consequences in Silicon Valley before voters decide its fate on Nov. 3.

Meta Platforms recently struck an agreement with CEO Mark Zuckerberg designed to keep him in California for eight years while giving him greater flexibility to sell non-voting shares if Proposition 40 leaves him facing a multibillion-dollar tax bill.

The ballot measure would impose a one-time 5% tax on Californians worth at least $1 billion, based on residency at the beginning of 2026. CalMatters estimates roughly 200 billionaires could be affected. Supporters say the money would primarily fund healthcare, along with education and food assistance.

Zuckerberg, whose net worth is estimated at about $240 billion, had considered moving his primary residence outside California if the proposal passes, according to Reuters.

Meta's solution involves its newly authorized Class C non-voting shares.

The arrangement allows Zuckerberg to sell a portion of those shares to potentially meet the tax obligation without surrendering the voting control he holds through Meta's Class B stock. He can immediately sell 20% of the Class C shares he receives, equivalent to 10% of his overall economic stake.

In return, Zuckerberg has committed to remain in California, or wherever Meta maintains its headquarters, and continue leading the company for eight years.

The debate extends beyond Zuckerberg.

Supporters of Proposition 40 argue that the tax could raise tens of billions of dollars for public services. Opponents argue it could encourage wealthy residents to relocate, reducing future income-tax collections and potentially affecting investment. Estimates of the ultimate fiscal impact vary widely and depend heavily on how billionaires respond.

Investor Takeaway

I think the investor significance is less about the politics of the tax itself and more about how wealth taxes can spill directly into corporate decisions.

Meta has effectively redesigned part of its capital structure partly to give Zuckerberg greater liquidity while preserving his control.

That makes Proposition 40 relevant not only to California tax policy, but also to executive retention, share issuance and corporate governance at some of the world's largest technology companies.

For Meta investors, the key things to watch are the Nov. 3 vote, Zuckerberg's share sales, the new Class C structure and whether similar arrangements emerge at other California companies.

Whatever voters ultimately decide, Meta's response shows that the proposal is already affecting boardroom decisions.

data.title: REG - Accel - KKR Co LLC Eleco PLC - Eleco plc Update on Letter of Intent
data.description:
RNS Number : 3156A Accel - KKR Company, LLC 23 October 2026  

NOT FOR RELEASE, PUBLICATION OR DISTRIBUTION IN WHOLE OR IN PART, DIRECTLY OR INDIRECTLY, IN, INTO OR FROM ANY JURISDICTION WHERE TO DO SO WOULD CONSTITUTE A VIOLATION OF THE RELEVANT LAWS OR REGULATIONS OF SUCH JURISDICTION

THIS ANNOUNCEMENT CONTAINS INSIDE INFORMATION

FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

23 October 2026

RECOMMENDED CASH ACQUISITION

of

ELECO PLC (“Eleco”)

by

AVOCET BIDCO LIMITED (“Bidco”)

(a newly formed company which will, as at the Effective Date, be indirectly wholly-owned by funds managed and/or advised by Accel-KKR and its affiliates)

to be implemented by means of a scheme of arrangement

under Part 26 of the Companies Act 2006

Update on Letter of Intent

On 10 September 2026, the board of directors of Bidco and Eleco made an announcement pursuant to Rule 2.7 of the Takeover Code (the “Rule 2.7 Announcement”) of a recommended all-cash acquisition by Bidco of the entire issued and to be issued ordinary share capital of Eleco (the “Acquisition”), intended to be implemented by means of a Court-sanctioned scheme of arrangement under Part 26 of the 2006 Act (the “Scheme”).

The circular in relation to the Scheme was published or made available to Eleco Shareholders on 2 October 2026 (the “Scheme Document”). Unless defined herein, defined terms shall have the meanings given to them in the Scheme Document.

As set out in the Rule 2.7 Announcement, Bidco had received a non-binding letter of intent from Raymond James Wealth Management Limited, trading as Charles Stanley (“Charles Stanley”) dated 8 September 2026 to exercise (or procure the exercise of) voting rights in favour of the resolutions relating to the Scheme and the Acquisition at the Meetings (or in the event that the Acquisition is implemented by an Offer, to accept or procure the acceptance of such Offer) in respect of 6,343,418 Eleco Shares, representing approximately 7.5 per cent. of the existing issued ordinary share capital of Eleco as at the last Business Day before the date of the Rule 2.7 Announcement (the “Charles Stanley Letter of Intent”).

Under the Charles Stanley Letter of Intent, Charles Stanley is permitted to sell, acquire or otherwise deal in Eleco Shares at any time.

As noted in the Update on Letter of Intent Announcement released by Bidco on 1 October 2026, Bidco became aware that Charles Stanley had sold a total of 765,127 Eleco Shares in the period between the Rule 2.7 Announcement and 29 September 2026.

As noted in the Update on Letter of Intent Announcement released by Bidco on 5 October 2026, Bidco became aware that Charles Stanley had sold a total of 9,660 Eleco Shares on 30 September 2026 and 42,340 Eleco Shares on 1 October 2026.

As noted in the Update on Letter of Intent Announcement released by Bidco on 7 October 2026, Bidco became aware that Charles Stanley had sold 98,280 Eleco Shares on 2 October 2026.

As noted in the Update on Letter of Intent Announcement released by Bidco on 8 October 2026, Bidco became aware that Charles Stanley had sold 4,300 and 103,185 Eleco Shares on 5 and 6 October 2026, respectively.

As noted in the Update on Letter of Intent Announcement released by Bidco on 12 October 2026, Bidco became aware that Charles Stanley had transferred out 9,500 Eleco Shares from its discretionary holding on 6 October 2026 and sold 204,860 Eleco Shares on 8 October 2026.

As noted in the Update on Letter of Intent Announcement released by Bidco on 13 October 2026, Bidco became aware that of the 24,980 Eleco Shares sold by Charles Stanley on 9 October 2026, 8,670 Eleco Shares were subject to the Charles Stanley Letter of Intent.

As noted in the Update on Letter of Intent Announcement released by Bidco on 14 October 2026, Bidco became aware that Charles Stanley had sold 3,610 Eleco Shares on 12 October 2026.

As noted in the Update on Letter of Intent Announcement released by Bidco on 15 October 2026, Bidco became aware that of the 645,810 Eleco Shares sold by Charles Stanley on 13 October 2026, 640,810 Eleco Shares were subject to the Charles Stanley Letter of Intent.

As noted in the Update on Letter of Intent Announcement released by Bidco on 19 October 2026, Bidco became aware that Charles Stanley had sold a total of 55,220 Eleco Shares since the previous Form 8.3 announcement released by Charles Stanley on 14 October 2026.

As noted in the Update on Letter of Intent Announcement released by Bidco on 22 October 2026, Bidco became aware that Charles Stanley had sold 374,050 Eleco Shares on 20 October 2026.

Pursuant to the Form 8.3 announcement released by Charles Stanley on 22 October 2026, Bidco became aware that of the 238,660 Eleco Shares sold by Charles Stanley on 21 October 2026, 13,660 Eleco Shares were subject to the Charles Stanley Letter of Intent.

Therefore, the total number of Eleco Shares which are subject to the Charles Stanley Letter of Intent has been reduced to 4,010,146 Eleco Shares, representing approximately 4.8 per cent. of the existing issued ordinary share capital of Eleco as at the close of business on the last Business Day prior to this announcement.

As a result, the total number of Eleco Shares which are subject to irrevocable undertakings and non-binding letters of intent to vote (or, where applicable, procure voting) in favour of the resolutions relating to the Scheme and the Acquisition at the Meetings (or in the event that the Acquisition is implemented by an Offer, to accept or procure the acceptance of such Offer) is 38,134,259 Eleco Shares, representing approximately 45.2 per cent. of the issued share capital of Eleco as at the close of business on the last Business Day prior to this announcement.
